pk.context: 500 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Bioavailability is about 70%, and food delays peak concentration with the tablet. Protein binding is 20% to 40%, and 40 to 50% of an oral dose is excreted unchanged in urine.
clues.substance: A hydrochloride monohydrate salt of a crystalline substance, with a molecular weight of 331.4 for the active moiety.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 250, 500 and 750 mg tablets, and a 500 mg oral dose is given every 12 hours.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects and worsened myasthenia gravis. Contraindicated with tizanidine; nausea and diarrhea are most common.
clues.indication: Skin, bone and joint, and complicated intra-abdominal infections; infectious diarrhea, typhoid fever, uncomplicated gonorrhea, inhalational anthrax exposure and plague.
clues.mechanism: It is bactericidal, inhibiting topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, enzymes needed for bacterial DNA replication.

tell: Its boxed warning for tendon rupture and peripheral neuropathy, with a 4-hour half-life, sets this fluoroquinolone apart.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Maximum serum concentrations are attained 1 to 2 hours after oral dosing
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The serum elimination half-life in subjects with normal renal function is approximately 4 hours
